CitizenBio: DH from Boston playing his farewell 2041 season. 436 career homers, six rings. Hit the home run that won the 2031 championship. Founded the Vinnie Keane West Oakland Baseball Academy in a rehabbed Mandela Parkway firehouse — free baseball at all levels. Born 2003, Boston. Designated hitter / outfielder, Oakland Athletics. 436 home runs. Six World Series rings. The heartbeat of the dynasty. Hit the home run that ended it in 2031 — nobody in the Coliseum sat down for nine minutes. Hal Richmond: "Keane is joy. He has always played with a quality that communicated pleasure in the act itself — not the result, not the celebration, but the swing, the moment of contact." Now in his farewell season alongside Kelley and Dillon. Bench role — his body has negotiated terms with the years. Opened the Vinnie Keane West Oakland Baseball Academy in a rehabbed firehouse on Mandela Parkway — free baseball for all levels. P Slayer: "the guy who made sure something was left on when he walked out." Sat courtside at Chase Center with Dillon, Aitken, and Paulson in Bulls colors — standing ovation. Preseason opener: .500/1HR/2H/4AB. Married to Amara Keane (veterinarian). Lives in Rockridge. The specific Oakland generosity — he has always been that.

CitizenBio: Born 1999, Oakland. Former Oakland Police Department public information officer who crossed over to journalism; the rank rides along as an earned credential, not a current commission, and the Tribune keeps it on her byline because it is the whole reason readers trust the copy. Covers crime, safety events and the OPD interface from Uptown. Writes incident analysis rather than incident reports — pursuit protocols, dispatch categories, what "no report filed" actually means — and interviews officers by name, age and years of service. Finds the story in the gap between what happened and how it got categorized. Masters degree, divorced, no children. A quarter-century across the two careers; last promoted C98. Her net worth outruns her Tribune salary several times over: the police years are still on the books.

Sabermetrics man who used to run a minor-league data blog, then spent years as Anthony Raines' statistical support — the name in the footnote of somebody else's column. Promoted C102 to the Tribune's citywide Data Desk, the paper's retrieval and verification seat across every beat: forty years of cleaning other people's numbers and, until that cycle, never once a byline of his own. Carries more net worth than his Tribune salary explains, from the years before the paper.

CitizenBio:
Jax Caldera is thirty-eight years old and technically homeless. He lists his address as Longfellow but he's been couch-surfing from Jingletown to Bushrod for two years. He got blacklisted from every alt-weekly in the Bay for being, in his words, "too mean to sacred cows." Now he only writes when he smells blood in the water.

He has no desk at the Tribune. Mags calls him when she needs someone to ask the question nobody else will ask. He shows up, files one piece, and disappears. His pieces are short, hot, and uncomfortable. He doesn't do follow-ups. He lights the match and walks away.

He has a master's degree in urban planning from Berkeley. He doesn't mention it. He'd rather you think he's just some loudmouth at a bar. The precision in his questions gives him away if you're paying attention.
